subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw add a native subagent spawn circuit breaker, and which scope, defaults, failure taxonomy, persistence model, and recovery controls should own it versus existing provider, session, and tool-loop breakers?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear from source, but the durable product contract crosses config schema, persisted state, spawn policy, operator alerts, UI/CLI status, provider fallback, and session health semantics.

options.title: Design a bounded core subagent breaker
options.body: Define failure classes, per-agent/task scope, conservative defaults, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override controls, and status surfacing before implementation.

options.title: Fold this into session health
options.body: Treat the subagent case as a specialization of the open gateway unhealthy-session breaker at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62615, preserving this issue as subagent evidence.

options.title: Keep this external for now
options.body: Continue relying on hooks/operator policy and existing provider/tool guards, but explicitly decline native subagent breaker state until stronger product direction exists.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded core subagent breaker
recommendation.body: Define failure classes, per-agent/task scope, conservative defaults, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override controls, and status surfacing before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest recent history across subagent registry, status, control boundaries, and lifecycle behavior relevant to choosing the durable owner boundary.
